title: The Barnacle That Kept Answering Back
story: On the drowned lighthouse reef, Mr 6 finds four fat clusters of Brinewallow crusted over the rescue boats, and every single cluster splits into two brand-new ones every six minutes. The ferry crew cannot chip the boats free for a full half hour. Mr 6 sheathes his sword, sits on a barrel, and does the smarter thing: he counts ahead.
question: If the 4 clusters double every 6 minutes for 30 minutes, and one salt-rune banishes exactly 8 clusters, how many salt-runes must Mr 6 carve?
solution: Each rune clears 8 clusters, so 128 / 8 = 16 salt-runes.
praise: Tracking the doublings was exactly the right move — the last step was turning those clusters into runes by dividing by 8.
hint: First ask: how many six-minute doubling steps fit inside 30 minutes? Only then worry about the runes.
victory: Mr 6 carves all sixteen runes before the first split even happens, and Brinewallow pops off the hulls in one salty sigh — out-counted by a number who came prepared.
imagePrompt: A knightly numeral 6 in a blue cape sitting calmly on a barrel carving glowing salt-runes while clusters of barnacles multiply across a wrecked lighthouse reef at low tide, silver mist and dawn light.
